title: You're one of 74 soldiers about to destroy a bridge... by walking.
formula: Strange act (stomping on purpose) -> why (it bounces, it's funny) -> escalation chain (whistle, stomp on the beat) -> the snap -> consequence -> You see + swing analogy -> what changed -> callback punch
facts: 12 April 1831, Broughton Suspension Bridge over the River Irwell, Salford near Manchester; opened 1826.
Suspension bridges were then called the 'new wonder of the age'; the bridge was a source of local pride.
A detachment of 74 men of the 60th Rifle Corps, returning to barracks from exercises on Kersal Moor, marching four abreast.
They felt it vibrate in time with their steps, found it amusing, whistled a marching tune and stepped to 'humour it'.
Near the far side they heard a sound like an irregular discharge of firearms; an iron column fell and the corner dropped 16-18 ft into the river.
About 40 men thrown into water about 2 ft deep; no deaths; 20 injured.
Investigation: a single badly forged bolt in a stay chain snapped; the bridge would likely have failed eventually anyway.
Result: the British Army ordered troops to break step when crossing bridges; 'break step' signs still exist (e.g. Albert Bridge, London).

lines.narration: You're stomping across a bridge on purpose, with 73 other *soldiers*.
lines.spoken: You're stomping across a bridge on purpose, with seventy-three other soldiers.
lines.scene: Cold open: a chain suspension bridge mid-bounce, the deck bent like a wave; a column of stickmen in dark rifle-green jackets and tall caps stamping in sync, you in the front row with a rust-orange sash.
lines.camera: Low angle from the riverbank, slow push-in
lines.gag: The bridge wobbles like jelly under the boots

lines.narration: Because the bridge is bouncing in time with your feet, and all of you think it's *hilarious*.
lines.scene: Faces down the column: grins, a soldier bobbing up and down with his cheeks puffed, caps bouncing.
lines.camera: Lateral glide along the grinning faces
lines.gag: Every cap bobs in perfect unison

lines.narration: It's the town's pride, a bridge hanging from iron chains, the wonder of the *age*.
lines.scene: Wide: the bridge hanging between two stone towers over a brown river; townsfolk in top hats on the bank, one admiring the chains through a monocle.
lines.camera: Crane down from the sky past the chains
lines.gag: A townsman polishing a chain link with his sleeve

lines.narration: You're the 60th Rifles, marching home from drills, four abreast, in perfect *step*.
lines.spoken: You're the Sixtieth Rifles, marching home from drills, four abreast, in perfect step.
lines.scene: Ground level: rows of four boots land together on the planks; dust jumps on each beat.
lines.camera: Boot-level track with the column
lines.gag: Dust puffs jump off the planks on every beat

lines.narration: So somebody starts whistling a marching tune, and all 74 of you stomp right on the *beat*.
lines.spoken: So somebody starts whistling a marching tune, and all seventy-four of you stomp right on the beat.
lines.scene: A soldier whistles; music-note cards float out; the whole column lifts its knees and stamps harder.
lines.camera: Push-in on the whistler, then pull out to the column
lines.gag: Music notes bounce on the beat with the deck

lines.narration: Up goes the bridge. Down it comes. Up. *Down*.
lines.scene: Side view: the deck rises and falls under the column like a skipping rope; the river below sloshes with it.
lines.camera: Side-on, the camera bobs with the deck
lines.gag: A duck on the river bobs up and down in time with the bridge

lines.narration: And every step, it swings a little *higher*.
lines.scene: A glowing wave runs along the deck from boot to boot, bigger on each beat; the chains sway.
lines.camera: Slow tilt up as the wave grows
lines.gag: The bridge grows a sweat drop

lines.narration: Then, near the far end, there's a crack like somebody firing *guns*.
lines.scene: Smiles freeze mid-step. At the far tower, little spark lines flash around an iron column.
lines.camera: Hard cut to a punch close-up on your face, then whip to the column
lines.gag: A '!' pops over every head in the column at once

lines.narration: Before anyone can stop, an iron column *falls*.
lines.scene: The column tips over in slow motion (cut away before it lands).
lines.camera: Fast tilt down following the column

lines.narration: And the whole corner of the bridge drops 16 feet into the *river*.
lines.spoken: And the whole corner of the bridge drops sixteen feet into the river.
lines.scene: The deck corner swings down like a slide; soldiers slide off in a row into a wall of splash.
lines.camera: Impact kick on the splash
lines.gag: Soldiers slide off the deck like kids on a water slide

lines.narration: Luckily, the river is only 2 feet *deep*.
lines.spoken: [relieved] Luckily, the river is only two feet deep.
lines.scene: You standing in the river, water at your knees, cap floating past.
lines.camera: Slow pull-out
lines.gag: You look down at the tiny water level, relieved

lines.narration: Unluckily, the river is only 2 feet *deep*.
lines.spoken: [deadpan] Unluckily, the river is only two feet deep.
lines.scene: Same shot: a second soldier lands next to you bum-first. Ow-stars circle his head.
lines.camera: Same framing, hard cut

lines.narration: About 40 of you go in, 20 get hurt, and somehow, nobody *dies*.
lines.spoken: [amazed] About forty of you go in, twenty get hurt, and somehow, nobody dies.
lines.scene: Soldiers sitting in the shallow river, bandaged, a few arm slings; townsfolk wading in to help.
lines.camera: Wide drift along the river
lines.gag: One townsman brings a single towel for forty men

lines.narration: You see, a bridge is like a kid on a *swing*.
lines.scene: Analogy mini-scene in a sunny park: you push a small kid on a swing (two ropes, wide plank, clear frame).
lines.camera: Arc around the swing
lines.gag: The kid on the swing is wearing a tiny soldier's cap

lines.narration: Push at random, and nothing happens. Push at the right moment, every time, and it goes higher, and *higher*.
lines.scene: Your pushes land on the beat; a glowing arc traces each swing, bigger every time.
lines.camera: Follow the swing up, tilt to the sky
lines.gag: The swing loops right over the top bar

lines.narration: 74 soldiers on the beat is the best-timed push a bridge has ever *felt*.
lines.spoken: Seventy-four soldiers on the beat is the best-timed push a bridge has ever felt.
lines.scene: Match cut: the swing becomes the bridge, the marching column becomes the push.
lines.camera: Match cut from swing to bridge, push-in
lines.gag: The bridge, with a face, looks up at the column in horror

lines.narration: To be fair, one bolt was badly made, and it would have snapped *eventually*.
lines.scene: Macro insert: an investigator's magnifying glass on a tiny cracked bolt in a chain link.
lines.camera: Macro push-in on the bolt
lines.gag: The bolt gives a sad little shrug

lines.narration: You just made eventually happen *today*.
lines.scene: Back to you in the river, soaked, cap dripping, one sheepish grin.
lines.camera: Push-in on your face

lines.narration: So the army makes a new rule: when soldiers cross a bridge, they break *step*.
lines.scene: An officer nails a painted sign to a bridge post: 'TROOPS MUST BREAK STEP'. Each hammer blow makes the sign bounce.
lines.camera: Low angle push on the sign
lines.gag: The sign bounces in time with the hammer

lines.narration: Nearly 200 years later, a bridge in London still has that *sign*,
lines.spoken: [amused] Nearly two hundred years later, a bridge in London still has that sign,
lines.scene: Dissolve: the same sign, old and weathered, on a painted modern London bridge with traffic.
lines.camera: Fast pull-out from the sign with motion-blur streaks
lines.gag: A jogger crosses the modern bridge perfectly in step; the sign shakes

lines.narration: telling soldiers not to do what *you* did.
lines.scene: Dissolve back to 1831: you in the river, soaked, holding up your floating cap, smug grin on 'you'.
lines.camera: Push-in on your face, end on the word
lines.gag: Your cap pours out a stream of river water
